historical_claims.anchor: On his thirtieth birthday, Josef K. wakes in the furnished room where he has been living and finds that breakfast has not arrived.
The novel was left unfinished by Franz Kafka and published after his death.
There is an apparent acquittal, by which a defendant may be released for the moment without the case truly disappearing.
The doorkeeper tells him that it was intended for him alone and that it will now be closed.
The men take him to a deserted quarry.

work.note: The existing survey and claim 032000-c02 date posthumous publication to 1925. Composition in 1914–1915 is a separate fact, not the selected sort date.

description: Retells Kafka’s unfinished The Trial through Josef K.’s unexplained arrest, court offices embedded in ordinary life, dependence on lawyers, Titorelli’s distinction between final acquittal, apparent acquittal and protraction, and the cathedral parable Before the Law. Follows the execution without supplying a charge, verdict, or author-approved complete chapter order.
